paragraphs: S²TS-LLM addresses a mismatch between language models and time series: meaningful temporal patterns often span consecutive measurements, whereas text is organized around tokens. Simply describing measurements in words can also struggle to capture the variety of possible signals. The paper therefore changes both how a time series is represented and how its context is organized before asking a language model to analyze it.

The first component converts the signal into frequency-domain features, using a fixed number of components and prominent amplitudes. A limited vocabulary of symbols can then summarize key frequency patterns. The second component groups the sequence into blocks according to temporal patterns and adjusts positional encodings to reflect those groups. Together, these steps make signal content and temporal organization more compatible with the model's input structure.

The reported experiments find that this framework outperforms state-of-the-art methods across time-series tasks. The contribution is a coordinated representation strategy: symbolization abstracts frequency information, while segmentation addresses how neighboring observations carry meaning. These findings support repurposing language models for time-series analysis through both changes.
neurips-2025-bridging-time-and-linguisti.tldr: S²TS-LLM combines frequency-based symbols and temporal segmentation to improve language-model analysis of time series.

paragraphs: VGER tackles the problem of generating motion that respects an environment's geometry when the only input is one RGB image. A conventional route estimates depth from that image, but the paper identifies frustum-shaped errors in such estimates as a difficulty for downstream motion generation. Its alternative uses a video-generation model to construct additional views of the scene.

Starting from the image, the framework generates a video depicting a moving camera. The resulting frames become a multiview dataset for a pretrained 3D model, which produces a dense point cloud. A multiscale noise approach then supports training an implicit representation of the environment. The motion-generation model is built to follow the geometry represented through this process.

Evaluations across indoor and outdoor environments demonstrate smooth motions that account for the captured scene geometry. The central contribution connects generated visual viewpoints, 3D reconstruction, and motion generation in one pipeline. Its demonstrated outcome concerns consistency with the reconstructed representation: the additional viewpoints are generated from the original image, and the resulting geometry guides the motions.
neurips-2025-building-3d-representations.tldr: VGER turns one image into generated camera views, reconstructs scene geometry, and uses that representation to generate smooth, geometry-aware motions.

paragraphs: CellCLIP studies how to connect cellular images with the interventions that produced their visible changes. Cell Painting collects microscopy images at large scale, creating opportunities to compare how different perturbations affect cellular appearance. The challenge is that these images carry different meanings from everyday photographs, and interventions such as small molecules and gene knockouts are difficult to represent together.

The framework learns a shared representation of microscopy images and natural-language descriptions of perturbations through contrastive learning. Its image side combines pretrained encoders with a new channel-encoding scheme designed to capture relationships among microscopy channels. Its language side represents the perturbations, providing a common way to describe different intervention classes. This arrangement links what was done to a cell with its observed morphological response.

The authors report better performance than current open-source models on cross-modal retrieval and biologically meaningful downstream tasks, alongside substantial computation-time reductions. Retrieval tests assess the alignment between the two kinds of information, while downstream tasks address biological usefulness. Together, these findings support adapting image-language learning specifically to the structure of microscopy data.
neurips-2025-cellclip-learning-perturbat.tldr: CellCLIP aligns microscopy images with text descriptions of perturbations, improving reported biological-task performance and computational efficiency.

paragraphs: This paper introduces object tracking that combines visible images, depth, and thermal infrared signals. Existing approaches commonly use only two of these modalities, leaving challenges in complex scenes. The work supplies both a dataset for studying the three-modality setting and a tracker designed to combine the complementary information without discarding an existing RGB tracking model.

The RGBDT500 dataset contains 500 videos with synchronized frames across all three modalities. The images are spatially aligned, and object bounding boxes provide tracking annotations. The proposed tracker, RDTTrack, first combines thermal and depth information under an orthogonal projection constraint. It then supplies the combined information alongside RGB as prompts to a pretrained RGB-only tracker.

This design makes prompt learning the connection between additional sensors and an established tracking model. Experiments report significant improvements in accuracy and robustness over existing dual-modal approaches in complex scenarios. The dataset makes the new tracking setting available for further study, while the algorithm demonstrates how a pretrained visual tracker can incorporate two additional sources of information.
neurips-2025-collaborating-vision-depth-.tldr: RGBDT500 and RDTTrack combine aligned RGB, depth, and thermal data to improve reported tracking accuracy and robustness.

paragraphs: SIGMA connects discovering causal structure with identifying and estimating mediation pathways: the routes through which one variable may affect another. Traditional mediation analysis relies on pathways specified beforehand, while causal discovery can produce complex structures without directly interpreting their mediation effects. The framework addresses this separation by carrying uncertainty about structure through to the final effect estimates.

It uses differentiable Flow-Structural Equation Models to learn a distribution over causal structures and generate multiple directed acyclic graphs. A Path Stability Score evaluates how probable each pathway is across these possibilities, supporting selection of high-confidence paths. For those paths, Efficient Influence Functions and Bayesian model averaging combine estimation uncertainty within a structure with effect differences between structures.

Synthetic experiments report state-of-the-art pathway identification and effect quantification under structural uncertainty, multiple simultaneous pathways, and nonlinear relationships. In Human Phenotype Project data, SIGMA identifies mediation effects connecting sleep quality and cardiovascular health through inflammatory and metabolic pathways. The contribution is an integrated analysis in which uncertainty over causal routes remains relevant when estimating their effects.
neurips-2025-decoding-causal-structure-e.tldr: SIGMA discovers mediation pathways and estimates their effects while propagating uncertainty about the underlying causal structure.

paragraphs: DirectLayout focuses on arranging objects in 3D indoor scenes from text instructions. Improving individual object generation does not by itself solve where those objects should go. The paper identifies limited layout datasets and restrictive predefined constraints as obstacles to creating scenes that accommodate varied object descriptions and detailed user requests.

The framework uses a language model's spatial reasoning to generate numerical layouts directly. It first constructs a bird's-eye layout, lifts that arrangement into three dimensions, and refines object placements. Chain-of-thought activation using the 3D-Front dataset helps develop explicit reasoning about placement principles. A reasoning-grounded layout reward further supports generalization and spatial planning.

During inference, iterative asset-layout alignment uses in-context learning to address mismatches between the available assets and the generated arrangement. Experiments report strong semantic consistency, generalization, and physical plausibility. These findings support treating layout generation as a sequence of spatial reasoning decisions, with an additional adjustment process that connects planned placements to the objects actually used in the scene.
neurips-2025-direct-numerical-layout-gen.tldr: DirectLayout uses staged language-model spatial reasoning to generate and refine numerical 3D room layouts from text.

paragraphs: FR-JVE studies federated recommendation among subsidiaries, each holding its own users and items. This differs from a setting where each participating client is one person's device. Subsidiaries can have overlapping users alongside users unique to each business, so exchanging item representations alone does not capture all useful information. Directly uploading user information creates a privacy problem.

The framework transfers distilled rating preferences derived from each participant's local data. Before federated training, it reformats that data and uses model inversion with frozen user gradients to distill the preferences. A bridge function then aligns local preferences with aggregated global preferences on each client. A further matching step finds similar users to improve predictions for users shared across participants.

The authors analyze the method's privacy protection theoretically and report recommendation performance above state-of-the-art methods in their experiments. The contribution is a way to exchange useful preference knowledge in an organizational federation while addressing the complications of overlapping user populations. The privacy claim is framed as enhanced protection supported by analysis, rather than an unconditional promise about every deployment.
neurips-2025-efficient-knowledge-transfe.tldr: FR-JVE transfers distilled rating preferences across subsidiaries to improve federated recommendations while enhancing user privacy.

paragraphs: A single image can support several plausible explanations of an object's shape and material, especially when lighting is unknown. This paper takes inspiration from how small movements help people resolve that uncertainty. It introduces a conditional diffusion model that samples shape-and-material maps from a short video of an object undergoing small motions.

The architecture is parameter-efficient, trains directly in pixel space, and generates multiple disentangled object attributes together. Training uses a modest collection of synthetic object-motion videos with shape and material supervision. The generative formulation allows the output to represent several plausible interpretations of an observation, making uncertainty part of the prediction rather than forcing one explanation immediately.

For static observations, the model produces diverse predictions that reflect visual ambiguity. With motion, the predicted distributions concentrate around more accurate explanations. The authors also report high-quality estimates for less ambiguous real-world objects. These findings suggest a role for generative perception in embodied systems: continuous visual observations can help refine uncertain interpretations of an object's physical appearance.
neurips-2025-generative-perception-of-sh.tldr: A diffusion model represents ambiguous shape and material interpretations, then refines them using small object motions.

paragraphs: Implicit-ARAP addresses controlled editing of shapes represented by neural fields. These representations describe geometry continuously and compactly, but deforming them under spatial constraints presents a difficult balance between surface quality, robustness, and speed. The paper uses handle-guided deformation, where selected spatial controls guide the change in shape.

Its central construction is a local patch mesh that supplies discrete surface geometry for optimizing an As-Rigid-As-Possible deformation objective. The patches are built by projecting and deforming initially flat meshes onto level sets of a neural signed distance field. This process uses only the field and its gradient. It connects a continuous neural representation to a classical geometric objective through local surface discretization.

The evaluation reports consistent improvements over baselines in deformation quality, robustness, and computational efficiency. Additional experiments motivate the chosen discretization compared with marching cubes. The broader contribution is a practical connection between neural shape representations and established geometry-processing methods. The demonstrated task is deformation, while extending the same connection to other geometric tasks is presented as a future possibility.
neurips-2025-implicit-arap-efficient-han.tldr: Implicit-ARAP uses local surface meshes to deform neural fields with improved reported quality, robustness, and efficiency.

paragraphs: KINDLE aims to infer gene regulatory networks without requiring prior biological information when making predictions. Expression-only methods face a vast space of possible interactions, while methods constrained by prior knowledge depend on that knowledge's accuracy and can restrict discovery. The paper seeks to retain the benefit of existing knowledge while reducing this dependence at inference time.

Its three-stage framework trains a teacher that combines prior knowledge with temporal gene-expression dynamics, then distills the encoded knowledge into a student. The student infers networks from expression data alone. Thus, prior knowledge contributes during learning, but the final inference model does not need access to it. This distinction is central to the paper's use of prior-free inference.

KINDLE reports state-of-the-art performance on four benchmark datasets. It identifies important transcription factors and their roles in mouse embryonic development, and predicts cell-fate transitions following Gata1 and Spi1 knockouts in mouse hematopoietic stem cell data. These validations support both accurate network inference and the potential to uncover biological mechanisms beyond a predefined set of interactions.
neurips-2025-kindle-knowledge-guided-dis.tldr: KINDLE distills a knowledge-informed teacher into a student that infers gene regulatory networks from expression data alone.

paragraphs: nvBench 2.0 studies a common difficulty in generating charts from language: a user's request may reasonably correspond to more than one visualization. The benchmark is designed around this ambiguity, giving systems a setting in which interpreting an imprecise request is part of the task. It includes 7,878 queries and 24,076 visualizations from 780 tables spanning 153 domains.

The dataset starts with unambiguous seed visualizations and works backward to create queries with selected ambiguities. This controlled process produces multiple valid interpretations while preserving stepwise reasoning paths that connect queries to their corresponding visualizations. Those paths make the alternative interpretations traceable within the benchmark's construction.

The authors evaluate language models on these tasks and introduce Step-Text2Vis, a model trained on the benchmark using stepwise preference optimization. It outperforms all evaluated baselines for ambiguous text-to-visualization tasks. The combined contribution is an evaluation resource that explicitly represents multiple valid readings and a training approach that improves how a model reasons through those readings.
neurips-2025-nvbench-2-0-resolving-ambig.tldr: nvBench 2.0 evaluates ambiguous chart requests, and Step-Text2Vis improves results through stepwise preference optimization.

paragraphs: This paper studies how to choose weight decay and batch size as language-model pretraining grows. These settings interact with learning rate, model size, and dataset size, making rules for transferring them across training runs valuable. The authors examine the AdamW timescale, defined as batch size divided by the product of learning rate, weight decay, and dataset size.

For fixed model and dataset sizes, they verify the implication that optimal weight decay scales linearly with batch size. When model and dataset sizes change, however, the optimal timescale follows a power law in tokens per parameter. That relationship provides a method for predicting optimal weight decay before a larger training run.

The paper also separates the batch size that minimizes loss from the critical batch size beyond which additional data parallelism becomes ineffective. Both follow power laws in dataset size, independent of model size in the reported findings. The authors then analyze how these relationships inform choices of model and dataset size when both training time and compute matter.
neurips-2025-power-lines-scaling-laws-fo.tldr: The paper derives scaling relationships for weight decay and batch size that inform efficient language-model pretraining.

paragraphs: RMBoost addresses the loss of classification accuracy that boosting methods can experience when training labels are wrong. Existing robust approaches offer guarantees for some noise types, but the paper identifies gaps around realistic noise and finite datasets. It also notes that robustness methods can deliver unsatisfactory accuracy even when labels are clean.

The proposed robust minimax boosting methods minimize worst-case error probabilities and address general types of label noise. Their theoretical analysis provides finite-sample guarantees, making the number of available training examples part of the performance statement. The guarantees relate performance both to the error achieved without label noise and to Bayes risk, the best possible error.

These two reference points connect resistance to corrupted labels with the broader goal of accurate classification. Experiments support the theoretical direction: RMBoost remains resilient to label noise while also providing strong classification accuracy. The contribution combines a worst-case optimization approach with guarantees relevant to finite training sets and empirical evidence that robustness can accompany effective prediction.
neurips-2025-robust-minimax-boosting-wit.tldr: RMBoost minimizes worst-case classification error and provides finite-sample guarantees for learning with general label noise.

paragraphs: Model fingerprinting helps owners identify a shared language model through API access. This paper argues that the number of fingerprints a model can carry is important for reducing false discoveries, handling leaked fingerprints, and resisting groups of users trying to evade detection. It treats scalability as a security-relevant property of a fingerprinting scheme.

The authors introduce Perinucleus sampling to generate fingerprints intended to be scalable, persistent, and harmless. Their experiments embed 24,576 fingerprints into Llama-3.1-8B, two orders of magnitude more than existing schemes, without observed degradation of model utility. The inserted fingerprints also remain after supervised fine-tuning on standard post-training data.

The paper supplements this large-scale demonstration with theoretical and empirical analysis of security risks and how scalable fingerprinting can mitigate them. The findings connect capacity to practical identification: a model can retain many identifiers while continuing to perform its ordinary tasks in the tested setting. Persistence through the evaluated fine-tuning process further supports the usefulness of those identifiers after subsequent training.
neurips-2025-scalable-fingerprinting-of-.tldr: Perinucleus sampling embeds thousands of persistent model fingerprints without reported utility loss and helps mitigate fingerprinting security risks.

paragraphs: SOPHIA develops extended reasoning in vision-language models by combining their own visual understanding with reasoning from a language model. The paper identifies two obstacles: learning solely from a model's current behavior can restrict exploration, while copying external reasoning can introduce visual hallucinations when models perceive an image differently.

Its semi-off-policy behavior model uses visual understanding from the trainable vision-language model and slow-thinking reasoning from a separate language model. It assigns rewards based on reasoning outcomes and propagates visual rewards backward. The resulting trajectories and propagated rewards then train the vision-language model through off-policy reinforcement learning, connecting external reasoning ability with its own perception.

Experiments with InternVL2.5 and InternVL3.0 at 8B and 38B sizes support the approach. InternVL3.0-38B improves by a reported average of 8.50% and reaches leading open-source performance across multiple reasoning benchmarks. It also exceeds some closed-source models on MathVision and OlympiadBench. Further analysis finds advantages over supervised fine-tuning and direct on-policy learning, including a better starting policy for additional on-policy training.
neurips-2025-semi-off-policy-reinforceme.tldr: SOPHIA combines a vision-language model's perception with external language-model reasoning to improve multimodal reasoning through reinforcement learning.

paragraphs: This paper studies stochastic shortest-path learning with adversarial costs and full-information feedback. Its focus is sparsity: only M state-action pairs incur costs, even though the full space contains SA pairs. The question is whether learning guarantees can reflect the smaller number of costly pairs instead of the size of the entire problem.

When transition dynamics are known, standard online mirror descent with negative-entropy regularization has a square-root logarithmic dependence on SA. The authors show that this dependence is worst-case optimal, but that negative entropy cannot adapt adequately to sparse costs. They introduce a family of l_r-norm regularizers, with r between one and two, that replaces this dependence with the square root of log M.

A matching lower bound establishes optimality of the sparsity dependence. The distinction between known and unknown transitions is essential: when transitions must also be learned, the authors prove that minimax regret still depends polynomially on SA, even with sparse costs. Sparsity therefore reduces the effective dimension in the known-transition setting, with substantially more limited benefits in the unknown-transition setting.
neurips-2025-stochastic-shortest-path-wi.tldr: New regularizers exploit sparse costs optimally when transitions are known, while unknown transitions retain substantial state-action dependence.

paragraphs: This paper models a news service that receives a stream of items and must present up to k of them whenever a user visits. Each displayed item has a probability of being consumed and covers particular topics. The objective is to maximize expected total topic coverage while accommodating visits whose timing is not fixed in advance.

The authors connect this problem to submodular maximization under a matroid constraint. Existing methods can be adapted when the visit count is known beforehand or memory can grow linearly with the stream. However, those methods lose bounded performance guarantees when only an upper bound on visits is available and memory must remain sublinear.

The proposed online streaming algorithm addresses that harder setting with a competitive guarantee controlled by an approximation-quality parameter. It processes the stream once and requires memory independent of stream length. Empirical results also show consistent improvements over baselines. The contribution combines a coverage objective that accounts for uncertain consumption with an algorithm suited to unpredictable demand and restricted storage.
neurips-2025-streaming-stochastic-submod.tldr: A single-pass streaming algorithm provides guaranteed expected topic coverage under uncertain user visits with memory independent of stream length.

paragraphs: Succeed or Learn Slowly, or SoLS, improves reinforcement learning for foundation models controlling mobile apps across multiple steps. Such tasks can provide sparse rewards, making useful learning signals difficult to obtain. The paper's central observation is asymmetric: high-return positive samples typically do not need policy regularization, while updates from negative samples can damage model performance.

SoLS modifies an off-policy actor-critic approach to treat those cases differently. Positive samples receive direct policy updates, while negative samples receive conservative, regularized updates intended to prevent degradation. Successful Transition Replay adds a second mechanism by prioritizing learning from successful interactions. Both choices focus learning on experience that helps the navigation policy improve efficiently.

On AndroidWorld, SoLS reports at least a 17% relative improvement over existing methods, including prompting and reinforcement-learning approaches. It also requires substantially fewer computational resources than GPT-4o-based methods, with inference reported as 5–60 times faster. These findings support using different update strengths for successful and unsuccessful experience when fine-tuning models for app control.
neurips-2025-succeed-or-learn-slowly-sam.tldr: SoLS learns directly from successful app interactions and cautiously from unsuccessful ones, improving reported navigation performance and efficiency.

paragraphs: This paper examines whether image watermarks remain reliable against removal methods that alter semantic content. Watermarks embed imperceptible signals to support detection and provenance verification. Although semantic-level watermarking can resist conventional pixel-level attacks, that resistance does not establish how it behaves against strategies designed to change the image at a semantic level.

The proposed Next Frame Prediction Attack frames removal as video generation. It treats the watermarked image as an initial frame and generates a subsequent frame with subtle semantic changes, aiming to remove the watermark while preserving image quality. The conceptual shift is to use a generated continuation of the image as the transformed output.

The authors evaluate the approach against eight state-of-the-art watermarking schemes and compare it with thirteen removal-attack baselines. They report a consistently better trade-off between removing the watermark and maintaining image quality. These results expose vulnerabilities in the evaluated watermarking methods and motivate stronger designs. The central finding concerns robustness under a different class of transformation, beyond the conventional pixel-level attacks emphasized in earlier evaluations.
neurips-2025-the-future-unmarked-waterma.tldr: Next-frame prediction exposes vulnerabilities in evaluated image watermarks by improving the trade-off between removal and image quality.

paragraphs: TTA-VLM examines whether test-time adaptation delivers meaningful improvements for vision-language models. These methods adapt during inference without additional labeled data, but inconsistent settings and narrow evaluation can obscure their practical value. The paper introduces a unified, reproducible benchmark to make comparisons more informative.

The benchmark implements eight episodic and seven online adaptation methods across fifteen datasets. It evaluates both CLIP and SigLIP and includes training-time tuning methods to test how adaptation interacts with prior tuning. Assessment extends beyond classification accuracy to robustness, calibration, out-of-distribution detection, and stability. This broader coverage makes it possible to examine whether higher accuracy accompanies other desirable model behavior.

The experiments find limited gains over pioneering work, poor collaboration between current adaptation methods and training-time fine-tuning, and frequent reductions in trustworthiness accompanying accuracy gains. These are findings about the evaluated methods and settings, rather than a claim that adaptation cannot improve. The contribution is both the comparison framework and evidence that accuracy alone can give an incomplete picture of progress.
neurips-2025-the-illusion-of-progress-a-.tldr: TTA-VLM finds limited recent adaptation gains and frequent trustworthiness trade-offs through a unified evaluation beyond accuracy.

paragraphs: The Omni-Expert aims to obtain the task-specialization benefits of a mixture of experts using a single expert model. Multiple experts can improve performance by dividing work among specialized components, but their computational demands can be difficult to accommodate in devices with strict resource and timing requirements. Cochlear implants provide the paper's motivating application.

The proposed method uses feature transformations to provide a divide-and-conquer capability within one model. The authors demonstrate it through phoneme-specific time-frequency masking for speech dereverberation in a cochlear implant setting. This task connects the approach to speech processing where reducing reverberation and keeping computation manageable are both relevant goals.

Across multiple speech datasets and reverberation levels, the Omni-Expert yields statistically significant improvements in objective intelligibility measures for cochlear-implant-vocoded speech. It also has substantially lower computational cost than a corresponding mixture-of-experts model. The evidence supports feature transformation as an efficient route to specialization in this application. The reported intelligibility findings concern objective measures of the processed speech.
neurips-2025-the-omni-expert-a-computati.tldr: The Omni-Expert uses feature transformations to deliver efficient specialization in a single model for cochlear-implant speech dereverberation.

paragraphs: This paper studies whether a coevolutionary algorithm can reliably retain a strict Nash equilibrium after finding it. Methods that operate across an entire action space can become infeasible when there are too many actions to examine. Randomized search offers an alternative, but has lacked many of the theoretical guarantees available for exhaustive methods.

The authors develop a method for proving necessary and sufficient conditions for stability, defined here as reliably retaining an equilibrium following discovery. That focus separates the question of keeping an equilibrium from the question of locating one. The resulting bounds are adapted to the application and the particular algorithm instance, allowing them to inform parameter configuration.

The work also shows how regret bounds can be deduced from its results and includes corresponding empirical analysis. Its contribution is a framework for understanding retention behavior in randomized coevolutionary search. By connecting stability conditions to concrete algorithm settings, the analysis provides a practical route for configuring such methods when exhaustive action-space procedures are unsuitable.
neurips-2025-theoretical-guarantees-for-.tldr: The paper develops necessary and sufficient stability conditions for coevolutionary algorithms to retain discovered strict Nash equilibria.

paragraphs: This paper reinterprets guidance in text-to-image diffusion as a fixed-point iteration problem. Its target is a latent path that produces consistent outputs under conditional and unconditional generation. The authors argue that differing theoretical accounts of classifier-free guidance have obscured design choices, and offer this shared perspective as a basis for improving them.

Within that framework, classifier-free guidance and its variants correspond to single-step iterations over short intervals. The paper proves inefficiency for this form of iteration and introduces Foresight Guidance to change how effort is allocated. Foresight Guidance emphasizes longer-interval subproblems early in diffusion and uses more iterations for them, bringing a longer-range focus to the generation process.

Experiments across diverse datasets and model architectures report improvements over state-of-the-art methods in image quality and computational efficiency. The contribution therefore combines a theoretical interpretation with a concrete guidance procedure. Its findings support changing the intervals and iteration effort used during guidance, and motivate adaptive designs based on the same fixed-point perspective.
neurips-2025-towards-a-golden-classifier.tldr: Foresight Guidance uses a fixed-point view of diffusion guidance to improve reported image quality and computational efficiency.

paragraphs: This paper addresses generating new 3D molecules that satisfy several desired properties at once. Diffusion models can produce high-quality molecular structures, but controlling multiple objectives remains difficult. The proposed framework uses reinforcement learning to guide molecular diffusion models while also considering uncertainty in the property predictions used for optimization.

Surrogate models estimate molecular properties and their predictive uncertainty. Those estimates dynamically shape reward functions, helping balance the objectives during reinforcement learning. The framework is evaluated across three benchmark datasets and multiple diffusion architectures, where it consistently outperforms baselines in molecular quality and property optimization. This evaluation connects the reward design to improvements across several underlying generators.

The authors additionally examine leading candidates using molecular dynamics simulations and ADMET profiling. These analyses indicate promising drug-like behavior and binding stability comparable to known EGFR inhibitors. Those findings are computational evidence about generated candidates and support the approach's potential for automated molecular design. The central contribution is bringing uncertainty-aware rewards into the joint optimization of several molecular goals.
neurips-2025-uncertainty-aware-multi-obj.tldr: Uncertainty-aware reinforcement learning guides 3D molecular diffusion models toward multiple properties while improving reported molecular quality.

paragraphs: This paper studies two-player zero-sum stochastic games in which players have only partial observations. The aim is to compute strategies within an epsilon tolerance of optimality. A central obstacle has been the lack of a principled connection to dynamic-programming methods developed for stochastic games, making earlier transfers of those methods dependent on ad hoc constructions.

The authors introduce what they describe as the first lossless reduction to transition-independent zero-sum stochastic games. Lossless has a specific meaning here: the transformation preserves value functions, equilibrium strategies, and optimality structure. These preserved properties matter because they let solution methods operate on the transformed game while retaining the strategic content of the original problem.

Using this reduction, the authors apply point-based value iteration and empirically obtain epsilon-optimal strategies across several benchmark domains. Performance consistently matches or exceeds existing state-of-the-art methods in those evaluations. The broader contribution is a systematic connection between the two game settings, enabling a class of dynamic-programming techniques and associated theoretical ideas to transfer to partially observable problems.
neurips-2025-varepsilon-optimally-solvin.tldr: A lossless game reduction enables dynamic-programming methods to compute empirically epsilon-optimal strategies in partially observable zero-sum games.
